phases.title: Idea & Strategy
phases.introduction: Frame the opportunity, make assumptions explicit and authorize a bounded investment in Discovery.

phases.title: Discovery
phases.introduction: Establish evidence about the problem, solution concepts, demand, economics and feasibility, then record a cross-functional decision.

phases.title: Definition and Design
phases.introduction:
Define and validate the next useful product increment, its quality and technical approach, the brand and its route to market.

**Sequencing note:** 3.12 and 3.13 preserve the existing numbering; follow their dependencies rather than postponing this work until the end of phase 3.

phases.title: Development and Validation
phases.introduction: Build and validate increments, prepare operations and produce a release candidate with explicit readiness evidence.

phases.title: Launch
phases.introduction: Deploy and introduce the approved product to its intended audience, stabilize the launch and establish ongoing ownership.

phases.title: Operation and Evolution
phases.introduction: Operate the product continuously, learn from outcomes and deliver proportionate improvements through repeated iterations.

phases.title: Retirement or Replacement
phases.introduction: Carry out an authorized transition or closure while managing affected users, data, dependencies and residual obligations.

1.1.title: Initial ideation and opportunity assessment
1.1.deliverable: Shortlisted ideas, initial opportunity statements, selection criteria and rationale for the opportunity chosen for investigation.
1.1.exit_criteria: At least one opportunity has a clear problem hypothesis, intended beneficiary and selection rationale; rejected ideas and major unknowns are recorded.
1.1.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

1.2.title: Define product vision and strategic goals
1.2.deliverable: Product vision statement, strategic objectives, initial outcome metrics and guiding product principles.
1.2.exit_criteria: Vision, intended outcomes, strategic boundaries and initial success measures are understandable and agreed by the designated business and product decision owners.
1.2.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

1.3.title: Define initial target audience and value proposition
1.3.deliverable: Initial user and buyer segment hypotheses, problem statements, value proposition and differentiation hypotheses.
1.3.exit_criteria: Users and buyers are distinguished where relevant; the proposed problem, value and differentiation are explicit and assumptions are labelled.
1.3.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

1.4.title: Define the business model
1.4.deliverable: Initial business model, monetization and pricing hypotheses, cost structure and preliminary economic assumptions.
1.4.exit_criteria: The model explains value delivery, funding or revenue, major costs and critical dependencies, with assumptions and alternatives visible.
1.4.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

1.5.title: Identify strategic assumptions, risks and constraints
1.5.deliverable: Prioritized assumptions and risks, known constraints, initial data-use and licensing questions, validation priorities and decision criteria for continuing, changing direction or stopping.
1.5.exit_criteria: High-impact assumptions and constraints have owners, evidence status, an investigation priority and proposed decision criteria.
1.5.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

1.6.title: Define the initial budget and resource allocation
1.6.deliverable: Approved discovery budget, initial resource allocation, indicative timeline, funding assumptions and agreed investment review checkpoints.
1.6.exit_criteria: Discovery has an approved resource envelope, named capacity, review dates and an investment decision owner; funding conditions are explicit.
1.6.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

2.1.title: Market and user research
2.1.deliverable: Market and competitor analysis, initial user segmentation, stakeholder map, research findings and problem hypotheses.
2.1.exit_criteria: Relevant users, buyers, stakeholders and alternatives have been investigated with a documented method, sample, findings and limitations.
2.1.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

2.2.title: Problem validation
2.2.deliverable: Evidence-backed problem statements, prioritized user needs, findings that support or challenge the hypotheses, and remaining uncertainties.
2.2.exit_criteria: Priority problems have evidence of significance and context, disconfirming findings and limitations are recorded, and a proceed/revise/stop recommendation is justified.
2.2.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

2.3.title: Explore solution concepts
2.3.deliverable: Solution concepts, candidate feature hypotheses, lightweight sketches or concept prototypes, early concept-test findings and a shortlist of options with remaining uncertainties.
2.3.exit_criteria: At least one promising concept has an explicit value hypothesis, initial user feedback, comparison with alternatives and visible unresolved risks.
2.3.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

2.4.title: Evaluate demand
2.4.deliverable: Demand-validation findings, evidence of adoption or purchase interest, initial acquisition-channel hypotheses, and documented limitations distinguishing stated intent from actual commitments.
2.4.exit_criteria: Adoption and, where relevant, purchase hypotheses have been tested against predefined criteria; evidence strength, sample and uncertainty are reported.
2.4.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

2.5.title: Evaluate economic viability and technical feasibility
2.5.deliverable: Preliminary business case, assumption-based unit economics and financial scenarios, initial technical feasibility assessment, consolidated Discovery evidence, major risks and a recorded decision to proceed, investigate further, reformulate or stop.
2.5.exit_criteria: The evidence and material uncertainties are consolidated; the designated product, business and technical decision owners record whether to proceed, investigate further, reformulate or stop, including any conditions.
2.5.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.1.title: Define scope and priorities
3.1.deliverable: Prioritized scope, explicit exclusions, initial product increment and rationale linking priorities to intended outcomes.
3.1.exit_criteria: Included and excluded scope, intended outcomes, priority rationale and the first useful increment are agreed; unresolved assumptions have owners.
3.1.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.2.title: Specify behaviour
3.2.deliverable: Functional requirements (FR), business rules, state and permission models, business flows, exception scenarios and acceptance criteria linked to the agreed scope.
3.2.exit_criteria: The next increment's critical behaviours, permissions, state transitions and exception cases are defined well enough to design and test; contradictions and blocking unknowns are resolved.
3.2.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.3.title: Define quality requirements
3.3.deliverable: Verifiable non-functional requirements (NFR), product-specific quality thresholds and test conditions, initial service and recovery objectives, and applicable security, accessibility and privacy requirements.
3.3.exit_criteria: Applicable quality requirements have measurable criteria, verification methods and owners; assumptions, cost implications and risk acceptance are explicit.
3.3.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.4.title: Design the experience (UX)
3.4.deliverable: Information architecture, user flows, and wireframes.
3.4.exit_criteria: Priority journeys and information structure cover normal and significant exception paths; the intended content and interaction logic are understandable for the next increment.
3.4.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.5.title: Design the user interface
3.5.deliverable: Visual designs, screen and component states, responsive specifications and a design system.
3.5.exit_criteria: Required screens, responsive behaviour and relevant component states are specified and reviewed for brand consistency, usability, accessibility and implementation feasibility.
3.5.applicability: Conditional on a visual product interface; reuse established design assets when appropriate. For headless services, document N/A and specify consumer-facing contracts in 3.2 and 3.6.

3.6.title: Design the technical solution
3.6.deliverable: Initial technical architecture, data model, API and integration contracts, data-flow and lifecycle specifications, security design and threat assessment, and documented technical decisions and trade-offs.
3.6.exit_criteria: The architecture supports the first increment and quality requirements; interfaces, data responsibilities and trade-offs are explicit, with critical design risks resolved or accepted by the relevant authority.
3.6.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.7.title: Align product & offer
3.7.deliverable: Product offering and packaging proposal, feature-to-plan mapping, positioning and messaging aligned with the product’s actual capabilities.
3.7.exit_criteria: The initial offer, packaging, claims and proposed pricing fit the scope and audience; required pricing decisions and unsupported promises are resolved or clearly pending with owners.
3.7.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.8.title: Prototype and validate the experience
3.8.deliverable: Tested prototypes, research findings and limitations, prioritized adjustments and a recorded decision on the proposed experience.
3.8.exit_criteria: Critical tasks and messages have been tested with relevant participants; significant findings are resolved, retested or explicitly accepted, with limitations documented.
3.8.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.9.title: Resolve technical uncertainty
3.9.deliverable: Technical feasibility findings, proof-of-concept results, recommended approaches, and remaining risks with mitigation actions.
3.9.exit_criteria: Each investigated critical assumption has a result, limitations and a decision; remaining risks have owners and do not silently invalidate the chosen implementation approach.
3.9.applicability: Conditional: focused spikes or proofs of concept are required only for material unresolved uncertainty. Otherwise record why existing evidence is sufficient.

3.10.title: Define measurement
3.10.deliverable: Measurement plan, metric definitions, analytics event specifications and an initial reporting plan.
3.10.exit_criteria: Priority outcomes have metric definitions, populations/windows, required events/data, ownership and decision use; collection is feasible and respects agreed data constraints.
3.10.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.11.title: Plan development
3.11.deliverable: Prioritized backlog, initial delivery plan, dependency map, effort estimates, resource allocation, risk-based validation approach and agreed acceptance and release criteria.
3.11.exit_criteria: The first increment has owners, workable dependencies, bounded estimates, acceptance criteria and a risk-based test/review approach; funding and capacity constraints are addressed.
3.11.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

3.12.title: Define brand identity and communication principles
3.12.deliverable: Brand brief, approved visual identity and tone-of-voice guidelines, initial brand assets, naming decisions where relevant and shared product/marketing usage principles.
3.12.exit_criteria: Brand voice, visual direction and usage principles are approved at the required depth; product and marketing can apply them consistently, with naming/licensing questions resolved where applicable.
3.12.applicability: Required at proportionate depth; adapt an existing brand where appropriate. Naming and full identity creation are conditional, not mandatory reinvention.

3.13.title: Define the go-to-market strategy
3.13.deliverable: GTM strategy, prioritized segments and channels, commercial motion, launch and lifecycle objectives, approved or explicitly pending budget assumptions, initial experiment portfolio and marketing readiness criteria.
3.13.exit_criteria: Initial segments, route to market, owners, budget status, launch/lifecycle objectives, experiments and readiness criteria are explicit and aligned with product capability and economics.
3.13.applicability: Required as a route-to-adoption plan; paid campaigns, sales motions, partnerships and external marketing apply only when relevant to the product.

4.1.title: Prepare development environments and delivery foundations
4.1.deliverable: Working development and testing environments, configured delivery pipelines, repository conventions and environment setup documentation.
4.1.exit_criteria: The team can build and test reproducibly with appropriate access, secret/configuration handling and automated checks; environment setup and ownership are documented.
4.1.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.2.title: Implement product features incrementally
4.2.deliverable: Working product increments, implementation-level tests, updated technical documentation and traceability to requirements.
4.2.exit_criteria: An increment implements the agreed behaviour and includes relevant tests and documentation; its change set is ready for the applicable review and validation activities.
4.2.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.3.title: Implement integrations and data handling
4.3.deliverable: Tested integrations and data flows, verified interface contracts, and migration or import procedures where applicable.
4.3.exit_criteria: Applicable integrations and data paths work under expected and significant failure conditions; contracts, reconciliation checks and recovery implications are documented and tested.
4.3.applicability: Required for applicable data handling and integrations; external-service, import and migration work is conditional on actual product needs.

4.4.title: Review code quality and maintainability
4.4.deliverable: Reviewed changes, automated quality-check results, documented technical decisions and tracked technical debt.
4.4.exit_criteria: Required peer and automated checks pass for the reviewed change; blocking findings are resolved and accepted debt or exceptions have owners.
4.4.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.5.title: Perform functional and regression testing
4.5.deliverable: Test results linked to requirements, reusable automated tests, defect reports and verified fixes.
4.5.exit_criteria: Critical behaviours and significant failure scenarios have evidence of correct operation; blocking defects are resolved and retested, with residual limitations recorded.
4.5.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.6.title: Validate non-functional requirements
4.6.deliverable: Non-functional validation results, identified limitations, remediation actions and documented residual risks.
4.6.exit_criteria: Applicable quality criteria are met under stated conditions or explicit, authorized exceptions exist; material limitations and corrective actions are visible.
4.6.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.7.title: Implement and verify security and privacy controls
4.7.deliverable: Implemented controls, security assessment findings, verified remediation evidence and documented unresolved risks with assigned owners.
4.7.exit_criteria: Required controls and significant findings have verification evidence; release-blocking findings are resolved, and residual risks have an authorized decision and accountable owner.
4.7.applicability: Required at proportionate depth; specialist assessments or independent testing are conditional on exposure, obligations and product risk.

4.8.title: Implement analytics and observability
4.8.deliverable: Validated analytics instrumentation, operational dashboards, configured alerts and measurement-quality checks.
4.8.exit_criteria: Critical events and operational signals are verified end to end in the available environment; dashboards, alert routing and sensitive-data handling meet agreed criteria.
4.8.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.9.title: Validate product acceptance and usability
4.9.deliverable: Product acceptance report, usability findings, prioritized adjustments and an explicit acceptance status for the release scope.
4.9.exit_criteria: Product acceptance is explicitly recorded for the release scope; critical user tasks work and material usability gaps are resolved or accepted with documented consequences.
4.9.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.10.title: Prepare operations and support
4.10.deliverable: Operational runbooks, support documentation, ownership and escalation paths, recovery procedures and training materials.
4.10.exit_criteria: Named operators can use the runbooks, alerts, escalation paths and support materials; necessary recovery checks and training are complete, with coverage and residual gaps explicit.
4.10.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

4.11.title: Verify release readiness
4.11.deliverable: Release candidate, consolidated readiness assessment, deployment and rollback plan, known-issues register and a recorded decision to proceed or address remaining blockers.
4.11.exit_criteria: The specific release candidate has a recorded technical readiness decision, domain sign-offs, deployment/recovery plan and no unresolved release blockers under agreed criteria.
4.11.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

5.1.title: Coordinate the launch and confirm readiness
5.1.deliverable: Integrated launch plan, ownership and dependency map, agreed launch criteria and a recorded readiness decision.
5.1.exit_criteria: The intended rollout stage has an owner, timing, audience, readiness evidence, dependencies, stop conditions and a recorded go/no-go decision.
5.1.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

5.2.title: Confirm legal, privacy and security readiness
5.2.deliverable: Reviewed legal materials, legal and security readiness assessments, documented outstanding issues and applicable release conditions.
5.2.exit_criteria: Applicable launch requirements are addressed or an authorized disposition is recorded; release-blocking issues are closed and the relevant notices, terms and controls are ready.
5.2.applicability: Required as an applicability/readiness check; the depth and specialist involvement depend on the product, audience, data and obligations.

5.3.title: Finalize marketing and launch design assets
5.3.deliverable: Launch website or landing pages, campaign creatives, product demonstrations, release notes, email and social content, and store listings where applicable.
5.3.exit_criteria: Required launch materials are accurate, accessible at the agreed level, consistent with the brand and ready in the needed formats and destinations.
5.3.applicability: Required at the appropriate scale; external campaigns, app-store listings, PR and specific creative formats are conditional.

5.4.title: Prepare acquisition and commercial channels
5.4.deliverable: Ready-to-activate acquisition channels, verified conversion paths, commercial materials and defined lead or sales handoffs.
5.4.exit_criteria: Relevant discovery-to-access/purchase paths, attribution, lead ownership and commercial handoffs are verified, with budget and activation authority recorded.
5.4.applicability: Required for relevant acquisition/adoption channels; paid media, sales, billing and CRM apply only where the business model needs them.

5.5.title: Deploy the approved release to production
5.5.deliverable: Deployed production release, deployment and migration records, production verification results and an operational rollback or recovery procedure.
5.5.exit_criteria: Production verification passes for the exposed scope, required migration checks succeed and a supported rollback or forward-recovery path is available.
5.5.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

5.6.title: Conduct a pilot or controlled rollout
5.6.deliverable: Pilot or rollout findings, prioritized issues, user feedback and a recorded decision on the next rollout stage.
5.6.exit_criteria: Pilot outcomes and limitations are recorded; predefined expansion criteria and technical/operational checks support an explicit expand, pause, revise or stop decision.
5.6.applicability: Conditional: use when risk, uncertainty, audience or deployment context benefits from limited exposure. Controlled production verification remains required even if a separate pilot is skipped.

5.7.title: Activate public launch and acquisition campaigns
5.7.deliverable: Published launch communications, active campaigns and commercial initiatives, and initial channel-performance results.
5.7.exit_criteria: Agreed communications and acquisition activities are live for the authorized audience, with owners, spend controls and functioning measurement.
5.7.applicability: Required as product availability/adoption communication; external public launch, paid campaigns and sales activation are conditional.

5.8.title: Onboard and support the first users
5.8.deliverable: Operational onboarding and support workflows, initial activation findings, support records and prioritized adoption issues.
5.8.exit_criteria: Initial users can obtain support and reach the intended first-value experience; major onboarding barriers and unresolved requests have owners and escalation paths.
5.8.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

5.9.title: Monitor and stabilize the launch
5.9.deliverable: Launch monitoring reports, incident and defect records, verified fixes and an explicit stabilization status.
5.9.exit_criteria: For the agreed observation window, launch-critical incidents are resolved or under an accepted plan, service criteria are satisfied and ongoing ownership is assigned.
5.9.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

5.10.title: Evaluate launch outcomes and transition to ongoing operations
5.10.deliverable: Launch review, initial performance baseline, prioritized improvement backlog, ongoing ownership assignments and an agreed transition to Operation and Evolution.
5.10.exit_criteria: The launch review records outcomes, limitations, outstanding work and named steady-state owners; operational transition is explicitly accepted.
5.10.applicability: Required; scale the depth to the product's uncertainty, impact and resources.

6.1.title: Operate and monitor the service
6.1.deliverable: Service-health dashboards, service-level reports, capacity assessments and operational records.
6.1.exit_criteria: Each operating review confirms service status, coverage and owned deviations from objectives; unresolved issues have an action or escalation.
6.1.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.2.title: Provide customer support and customer success
6.2.deliverable: Support resolutions, updated knowledge resources, customer-success plans where relevant, and categorized customer feedback.
6.2.exit_criteria: Requests in the work cycle are resolved, clearly communicated or assigned with next actions; recurring themes and customer risks are recorded.
6.2.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.3.title: Manage incidents and recovery
6.3.deliverable: Incident records, recovery verification, stakeholder communications, post-incident reviews and tracked corrective actions.
6.3.exit_criteria: Service or security impact is controlled, recovery is verified, communications are complete for the incident stage and significant follow-up actions have owners.
6.3.applicability: Event-driven when an incident occurs; response preparedness and appropriate exercises remain part of normal operational readiness.

6.4.title: Maintain technical health
6.4.deliverable: Maintenance updates, dependency and lifecycle tracking, prioritized technical-debt backlog and technical-health assessments.
6.4.exit_criteria: Scheduled maintenance changes are reviewed and verified, applicable compatibility risks are addressed and remaining debt has priority and ownership.
6.4.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.5.title: Maintain security, privacy and compliance
6.5.deliverable: Updated risk assessments, access reviews, vulnerability remediation records, control evidence and tracked compliance actions.
6.5.exit_criteria: Each review records control status, findings, owner decisions and remediation priorities; critical issues receive a timely response under the agreed process.
6.5.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.6.title: Measure product and business outcomes
6.6.deliverable: Product and business dashboards, cohort and funnel analyses, measurement-quality findings and evidence-based performance reviews.
6.6.exit_criteria: The review contains interpretable results, data-quality limitations and material changes, with sufficient context to support the stated decisions.
6.6.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.7.title: Improve adoption, retention and commercial growth
6.7.deliverable: Growth and retention initiatives, campaign and funnel improvements, commercial playbooks and measured outcomes.
6.7.exit_criteria: Each initiative has an evaluated outcome or justified continuation decision, with user impact, cost and evidence limitations visible.
6.7.applicability: Applicable to adoption and sustained customer value; paid growth, revenue expansion and renewal initiatives depend on the product's objectives and business model.

6.8.title: Conduct continuous discovery
6.8.deliverable: Updated research findings, opportunity backlog, revised hypotheses and supporting evidence for potential improvements.
6.8.exit_criteria: Investigated opportunities have evidence, an articulated problem, uncertainty and a decision on further research or consideration for delivery.
6.8.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.9.title: Prioritize the evolution roadmap
6.9.deliverable: Updated outcome-based roadmap, prioritized backlog, capacity allocation and documented prioritization decisions.
6.9.exit_criteria: The next work cycle has explicit priorities, rationale, scope boundaries, owners and capacity allocation, with mandatory remediation visible.
6.9.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.10.title: Deliver and evaluate improvements
6.10.deliverable: Released improvements, validation and experiment results, updated documentation and recorded follow-up decisions.
6.10.exit_criteria: The change has passed proportionate design, engineering, acceptance and release checks; its outcome is assessed or has an assigned observation plan.
6.10.applicability: Triggered by selected improvements or fixes; the depth of discovery, testing and rollout is tailored to the change's impact and uncertainty.

6.11.title: Optimize operational and economic efficiency
6.11.deliverable: Cost and unit-economics reviews, efficiency initiatives, updated forecasts and measured savings or productivity improvements.
6.11.exit_criteria: The review identifies feasible actions, baseline economics, owners and expected trade-offs; completed actions have measured outcomes where observable.
6.11.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

6.12.title: Review strategic direction and lifecycle decisions
6.12.deliverable: Strategic product review, updated investment decisions and direction, or an approved transition into Retirement or Replacement when appropriate.
6.12.exit_criteria: A direction and investment decision is recorded with evidence, conditions, owners and the next review trigger.
6.12.applicability: Ongoing while the product operates; apply the exit criterion to each review or work cycle, not to permanent completion of the activity.

7.1.title: Decide and approve retirement or replacement
7.1.deliverable: Approved retirement or replacement decision, scope, rationale and completion criteria.
7.1.exit_criteria: The authorized decision identifies the scope, affected parties, target conditions, funding/ownership and unresolved obligations for the transition.
7.1.applicability: Required once retirement or replacement is proposed; early project cancellation uses a proportionate closure path.

7.2.title: Plan and communicate the transition
7.2.deliverable: Transition plan, stakeholder communications, support arrangements and assigned responsibilities.
7.2.exit_criteria: Transition timing, notice requirements, owners, support, migration/exit options and acceptance criteria are approved; required communications are delivered or scheduled before affected actions.
7.2.applicability: Required for the affected scope; external notices and migration support depend on actual users, customers and commitments.

7.3.title: Transition users and data
7.3.deliverable: Verified migrations or exports, customer transition status and documented exceptions requiring follow-up.
7.3.exit_criteria: Required migrations or exports are verified, access and continuity checks pass where applicable, and remaining cases have an authorized disposition before source shutdown.
7.3.applicability: Conditional on affected users, workflows or data; record N/A and the supporting inventory if no transition/export is required.

7.4.title: Decommission the product securely
7.4.deliverable: Decommissioning records, data disposition records and verification that retired components and access are inactive.
7.4.exit_criteria: Retired components and obsolete access are inactive, shared dependencies remain functional and data archival/deletion actions are verified against the approved plan.
7.4.applicability: Required for deployed or provisioned product assets; tailor to actual infrastructure, accounts, integrations and retained data.

7.5.title: Complete commercial and operational closure
7.5.deliverable: Closure report, reconciled financial records, resolved or assigned obligations, archived documentation and lessons learned.
7.5.exit_criteria: Applicable billing/refunds and supplier actions are reconciled, unnecessary expenditure is stopped, residual obligations have owners and final closure is explicitly accepted.
7.5.applicability: Required at proportionate depth for every closed initiative or product; specific financial/contractual actions apply only where obligations exist.
